title: Tenant-aware multiplex query router and response stitcher to reduce dashboard tail latency
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Problem: Console dashboard query API exhibits long tail latency during high-concurrency tenant workloads and bursty scans (list/explore endpoints). Existing cursor pagination and shard-level caches reduce average latency but struggle with overlapping scans across tenants and time-windowed queries. This ticket implements a tenant-aware multiplexing router plus a response stitcher that collapses overlapping reads, reduces duplicate backend scans, and stitches partial results to honor existing cursor semantics while preserving correctness and stable ordering.
goals: Collapse redundant scan work when multiple near-simultaneous requests target overlapping key/time ranges for the same tenant
Introduce an orthogonal cache sharding strategy keyed by (tenant, time-window, fingerprint) to improve cache hit-rate for exploration queries
Implement a response stitcher that merges partial page results produced by multiplexed backends, preserving cursor stability and deterministic sort order
Reduce 95th/99th percentile latency for tenant dashboard list endpoints by at least 30% under mixed read/write load
Fail open to existing single-request path if multiplexing or stitching fails
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration tests demonstrating no cursor regressions for forward/backward pagination across stitched responses
Benchmark harness shows >=30% reduction in P95 latency on synthetic tenant burst scenarios compared to baseline
No increase in error rate for console APIs during canary (error budget preserved)
Feature gated behind runtime flag and observable via new multiplexing metrics in Console (multiplex_requests, stitched_pages, stitch_time_ms)
Graceful fallback to legacy router when dependencies (cache or stitcher) are disabled
design_notes: Router component will detect in-flight overlapping queries using a short-lived in-memory aggregation table keyed by (tenant_id, query_signature, time_window).
Query_signature includes sort keys, filter predicates, and page size to ensure stitchability. We will canonicalize filters to keep signature stability.
When overlap detected, the router batches requests into a single backend scan with a superset page window and returns per-request slices via the stitcher.
Orthogonal cache shard key: tenant_id|time_bucket(1m)|query_fingerprint. Cache entries store KV of page ranges to allow partial reuse.
Stitcher merges rows deterministically using stable sort keys and preserves opaque cursor tokens. Cursor encoding extended to include contributing segment metadata for validation on subsequent pages.
Speculative hedging: if backend doesn't return within X ms, send a parallel single-request path to avoid head-of-line blocking; reconcile duplicates in stitcher using request UUIDs.
We will add safety: per-tenant concurrency limits and backpressure to avoid head-of-line amplification under hot tenants.
Telemetry: instrument multiplexing_ratio, duplicate_scan_savings_tokens, average_stitch_latency_ms, failed_stitches_count.
We will keep the existing cursor protocol stable; any schema changes to cursors will be opt-in via release flag and compatible decoder.
Tradeoffs: adds complexity to router state and cursor encoding. But reduces backend IO and tail latency for common exploration patterns.
Open questions: optimal time_bucket size for different workloads, storage TTL for partial page caches, and upstream SDK behavior if opaque cursor tokens change. Plan to A/B test.
Related architecture note: complements adaptive KV caching work in ENG-761420; router will consult cache policies suggested by optimize service when available.
implementation_steps: Spike: implement prototype router/stitcher in a sandbox service with synthetic harness (2d)
Design review with Backend Platform and Console teams, gather feedback and finalize signature canonicalization (1d)
Implement router state store with non-blocking in-memory aggregation keyed by (tenant, signature) (3d)
Implement stitcher library to merge superset pages into per-request slices; unit tests for order determinism (4d)
Integrate orthogonal cache shard reads/writes and add eviction heuristics (3d)
End-to-end integration tests including cursor forward/backward, hedging reconciliation, and failure modes (3d)
Benchmarks: run load tests with synthetic tenant bursts and compare P95/P99 to baseline (2d)
Add telemetry and dashboard panels in Console for multiplexing metrics (2d)
Canary rollout: enable feature flag in staging -> canary cluster -> gradational rollout by tenant size (7 days monitoring)
Postmortem and follow-ups: tune bucket sizes and cache TTLs based on observed traffic (ongoing)
Docs: update API guarantees and cursor compatibility notes in Console docs and internal Confluence

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cursor token size grows due to contributing segment metadata. Mitigation: compress metadata and keep opt-in flag for extended cursor; fallback to legacy when token exceeds threshold.
Risk: Router state explosion for high-traffic tenants. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant aggregation limits and degrade to single-request path for super-hot tenants.
Risk: Incorrect stitching could reorder results for non-deterministic sorts. Mitigation: disallow multiplexing for queries with unstable sort keys; detect and fall back.
Risk: Increased memory pressure on edge routers. Mitigation: allocate bounded memory with LRU and fail-safe to legacy path when under pressure.
Risk: Operational complexity for debugging. Mitigation: add rich request-scoped trace IDs and stitch provenance in logs for troubleshooting.
